items.title: Mini Cooper Crash: High Court Judge Wants To Reduce Age Of Prosecuting Juveniles To 16 Years
points: A Kerala High Court judge has asked lawmakers to consider lowering the age at which young offenders are treated as juveniles from 18 to 16.
The observation came during a hearing about the alleged serving of alcohol to underage customers, following the Mini Cooper crash near Kochi airport that killed three people last month.
This was an observation made during court proceedings, not an amendment to the law or an order that all 16-year-olds must be prosecuted as adults.
The case arose after a Mini Cooper allegedly driven by 19-year-old Suhail Sajeev struck a scooter on the Airport-Athani road near Nedumbassery on October 11.
The judge's comments about 16-year-olds were therefore broader observations prompted by road-safety concerns, rather than a change in the legal treatment of this accused person.
It seeks accountability from excise officials and licensed bars for enforcing Kerala's rules against supplying alcohol to people below 23 years of age.

items.title: India-Canada free trade deal may be concluded next month, says Maninder Sidhu
points: Sidhu travelled to India for three days last week as the sixth round of negotiations commenced.
“India will be the next one that we’re going to get done,” he told reporters in Manila, where he was accompanying Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to the ASEAN Summit.
Sidhu travelled to Manila from India, where he spent three days and held a bilateral meeting with Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal in New Delhi.
Sidhu expressed optimism that the two countries would be able to “lock down” the agreement by next month, the deadline set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Carney for concluding negotiations.
Modi is scheduled to visit Canada in the second week of December, with the focus being on announcing the conclusion of the free trade agreement talks.

Sidhu stressed that in looking at the deal with India, Canada wasn’t just throwing a dart at a board, but had consulted with businesses, companies and chambers of commerce over the markets to which they sought access.

items.title: Kamarajar Port picks SBI Capital, IDBI Capital and ICICI Securities for IPO
points: Chennai-based Kamarajar Port Ltd has picked three investment banks for an initial public offering (IPO) that would make it India's first listed state-backed port.

The country's first corporate major port has hired SBI Capital Markets Ltd, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities Ltd, and ICICI Securities Ltd as the book-running lead managers for the offer, two people aware of the development told Mint.
The IPO is likely to include an offer for sale of about ₹1,200 crore, while a fresh issue could be decided at a later stage, a document issued by the port earlier in September showed.
Emails sent to Kamarajar Port, SBI Capital, IDBI Capital and ICICI Securities on 14 November did not elicit responses until press time.

Mint had reported on 13 September that the Chennai Port Authority, which wholly owns Kamarajar Port, had begun the process of seeking up to three bookrunning lead managers to structure and manage the issue.
The Centre originally held a 66.7% stake in Kamarajar, with the balance held by Chennai Port Authority.

items.title: Congress wants to contest 181 seats in 2027 UP polls, indicates Akhilesh
points: File | Photo Credit: ANI Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav indicated on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the Congress has expressed its wish to contest 181 seats in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, while asserting that the INDIA bloc would…
Asked at summit in Delhi whether the Congress is seeking to contest 100 seats, Mr. Yadav said the party has demanded more than that.

Asked if the demand was of 200 seats, he replied, "A little less than that." When the interviewer suggested 180 seats, Mr. Yadav said, "Add one more," indicating that the Congress has sought 181 seats from the SP.
He said he wants to thank the people of Faizabad, which includes Ayodhya, for their support to the SP in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.
SP's Awadesh Prasad won the Ayodhya Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 election.

items.title: Updated Mahindra Thar Roxx With DaVinci, OG Alloys Spotted Outside Dealer Showroom – Launch Soon
points: The updated Mahindra Thar Roxx has started reaching dealerships ahead of its expected launch.
An undisguised unit was spotted parked outside a Koncept Automobiles showroom, with fresh images from safarnamawithak showing its alloy wheels and giving us a closer look at the suspension.
The sighting follows earlier report, when a Thar Roxx test mule was spotted with camouflage around its wheels and underbody shots pointed to a DaVinci suspension upgrade.
Mahindra is yet to reveal which Roxx variants will get these alloys or whether the design will be offered alongside the existing wheel options.

The DaVinci update is expected to build on that with revised internal damper valving, aimed at improving bump absorption and body control.
The Thar Roxx is expected to continue with its existing 2.0-litre turbo-petrol and 2.2-litre diesel engines.

items.title: India votes against UNGA resolution calling for global moratorium on death penalty
points: File | Photo Credit: AP India has voted against a draft UN General Assembly resolution calling on nations to establish a moratorium on the death penalty.

The 193-member UNGA adopted, by recorded vote, the resolution on Friday (November 13, 2026) introduced by Mexico on ‘Moratorium on the use of the death penalty’, with 133 countries voting in favour of the resolution, 33 against and 16 abstentions.
India, along with Bahrain, China, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Japan, Kuwait, Maldives, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the U.S. , voted against the resolution.

The resolution expressed deep concern about the continued application of the death penalty and reaffirmed the right of all countries to develop their own legal systems, including determining appropriate legal penalties in accordance with international law.
It called upon all States to establish a moratorium on executions, with a view to abolishing the death penalty.

items.title: 25 shops gutted in fire at woollens market in Gurugram's Pataudi, no injuries reported
points: Around 25 shops were completely burned down on Sunday morning after a fire broke out here in the woollens market at the Ramlila Ground in Gurugram's Pataudi town, a fire officer said.
The fire spread so rapidly that the entire market was engulfed in flames in no time, the officer said.
On getting information, fire tenders from Pataudi and Manesar arrived at the scene and began firefighting operations.
No injuries have been reported in this incident, he added.
An official said that a woman in the area heard a noise at around 4 am and discovered that the market was on fire.
Local residents said that every year, from November to February, a woollens market is set up on the eastern part of Ramlila Maidan in Pataudi.
This year, it opened on November 4, under the aegis of the Himalayan Tribal Trade Association, and featured stalls run by vendors from Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.
According to the shopkeepers, each shop stocked winter clothing worth lakhs of rupees.

points: Women perform rituals on the occasion of Chhath Puja.

No case has been registered so far in connection with the incident, which occurred on Saturday (November 14, 2026) evening in the Nalasopara area, police said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
During the four-day Chhath festival, devotees gather at the waterbodies to offer prayers to the setting and rising sun.
Authorities had prohibited the rituals at the Nagela lake in the Gala Nagar area and locked its main entrance gate to enforce the restriction.
Devotees who arrived at the site for the festival were frustrated by the sudden closure.

points: File | Photo Credit: PTI On the 26th Jharkhand Foundation Day and the birth anniversary of tribal icon Birsa Munda, Chief Minister Hemant Soren urged people to resolve to "preserve the legacy of our brave ancestors, culture and identity" and build a…
"Today is a day of pride, self-respect and resolve for us," he posted on X.
The Chief Minister said the dream of a separate state was realised through the struggles, sacrifices and martyrdoms of many revolutionaries.
The leadership, struggles and contributions of Shibu Soren, martyrs Nirmal Mahato and Vinod Bihari Mahato, and countless movement activists are an invaluable legacy of Jharkhand's history.
Jharkhand, known for its pristine forests and natural resources, was created on this day in 2000, from what was previously the southern areas of Bihar.
Born in 1875 in Ulihatu village in Jharkhand's Khunti district, Birsa Munda is credited with mobilising tribals against colonial rule.
He died in British custody at the age of 25 on June 9, 1900.

items.title: Just Like That | A tale of two cities: Urban India’s moral and municipal abyss
points: If one wishes to understand the almost schizophrenia-inducing inequality that defines contemporary urban India, one need only read the newspapers from a single twenty-four-hour cycle in the National Capital Region.
Consider the grim ledger of November 10.
In Outer Delhi’s Ranhola area, four-year-old Imran vanished into the depths of a 50-foot-deep open sewer.
On that same afternoon, in Gurugram’s Sector 71, another preventable tragedy unfolded.

Official data tabled in the Delhi Assembly reveals a staggering indictment of civic apathy: in just two years, between 2024 and 2025, 89 citizens died across the national capital after falling into open drains or waterlogged underpasses.
In Gurugram’s upscale gated colonies, Resident Welfare Associations possess private budgets that dwarf the allocations of small municipalities.
Yet, the ultimate insulation from urban India’s collapse is not found in private real estate, but within the manicured avenues of Lutyens’ Delhi.

items.title: 5,000 Stubble Burning Cases Reported In Punjab, Rs 1 Crore Penalty Imposed
points: Punjab has recorded a total of 5,835 stubble burning incidents across 23 districts following the paddy harvest, with Patiala alone accounting for 391 cases, according to a report released by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), covering data…
The report revealed that out of the total incidents reported across the state, field-level inspections were carried out at 5,539 locations, confirming crop residue burning at 2,442 sites.
In Patiala district, 391 stubble burning incidents were reported, of which inspections were conducted at 356 locations.
A total penalty of Rs 8.35 lakh has been levied, out of which Rs 3.10 lakh has already been recovered, officials said.
The report further stated that 215 First Information Reports (FIRs) have been registered in Patiala district in connection with stubble burning incidents.
At the state level, the report highlighted that Environmental Compensation has been imposed in 2,152 cases across Punjab.
A cumulative penalty of Rs 1,08,55,000 has been levied under this action, of which Rs 40,40,000 has been recovered so far.

points: Aaron Vicky Thomas, son of the family, has taken delivery of three Rolls-Royce cars on the same day.
The collection comprises an ultra-luxurious two-tone Phantom and two Cullinan SUVs, with the combined value estimated at over Rs 50 crore.
The highlight of the collection is the two-tone Rolls-Royce Phantom, which reportedly features a gold Spirit of Ecstasy bonnet mascot.

items.title: Canadian Woman Flies To India To Marry Dating App Match. He Refuses Over Age
points: A Canadian woman who travelled thousands of kilometres to Rajasthan to marry a man she met on a dating app was left disappointed after he allegedly refused to go ahead with the marriage, prompting her to approach the Canadian Embassy.
The case came to light in Rajasthan's Neemrana in Kotputli-Behror district, where police were called in after the woman contacted the Canadian Embassy following a dispute over the proposed marriage.
According to Neemrana Station House Officer Surendra Yadav, the woman and Nitin, a resident of Panipat in Haryana, first connected through a dating app about a year ago.
Acting on those plans, the woman travelled to India on a tourist visa and arrived in Delhi on November 11.
During this period, discussions about the marriage moved forward, but matters took a different turn when her age, reportedly around 61, came to light.
Following the disagreement, the woman contacted the Canadian Embassy on November 13 and informed officials about the developments.

items.title: SHRESHTA 2027: Testing Agency Opens Applications For Class 9, 11 Admissions
points: SHRESHTA NETS 2027: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has opened the application window for the National Entrance Test for Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA NETS) 2027.
SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027 is conducted for SC & DNTs boys and girls to get admission to the best private residential schools in the country for admission to class 9th and 11th.
Applicants can apply for the SHRESHTA NETS 2027 through the official website, exams.nta.nic.in/shreshta.
The last date to apply for the exam is November 30, 2026 and there is no fee for online registration.
Once the registration window closes, the exam-conducting body will open an application correction window for applicants from December 2 to 4, 2026.
The examination will be conducted on January 10, 2027 and the city intimation slip for the same will be released on the portal on December 20, 2026.
A total of four sections will be there in the exam such as Mathematics, Science, Social Science and General Knowledge.

points: A metro ride on Bengaluru’s new Pink Line came with a light moment on Friday when Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar joked that he had no money with him, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid for his ticket.
The development came at a time when the state government and the Centre are at odds over the financing of Bengaluru’s metro expansion.

He swiped his card for me as well.” He was speaking to reporters during a separate metro ride from Kalena Agrahara to SG Palya when he made the remarks.

items.title: India’s commodity supply chains: Why market intelligence must translate into smarter logistics
points: India moved more goods in September 2026 than in any month before.
Over 141 million e-way bills were generated, the first time the count has crossed 140 million.
Yet these supply chains rarely break because India runs short of goods.
Decisions on which port to use, when a ship should arrive and how much storage and transport to book sit with the logistics team, which often learns about a big purchase only when the ships appear.
Refiners, also expecting strong festive sales, bought heavily for August and September, and imports reached an 11-month high of about 1.54 million tonne in August.
Oil came into the port faster than it left, the tanks filled, and by early September at least nine ships carrying over 3 lakh tonne were waiting outside Kandla, some for up to 10 days.
Better planning would not have built more tanks at Kandla, but it could have helped businesses spread out arrivals, send some ships to other ports or book storage elsewhere before the queue formed.

items.title: How to ensure that AI disruption doesn’t leave workers behind
points: Jay Clayton, a former U.S. attorney, is now—in the president’s words—America’s “AI czar.” More formally, he is head of the White House’s new Super Intelligence Force.
In that role, Clayton is responsible for developing “plans for responding to SI-enabled threats” to America.
That remit is a fine starting place for Washington, which, until very recently, been concerningly disengaged with regulating or overseeing the artificial-intelligence industry at all.
Attending to concerns around AI threats to privacy, national security, and perhaps even civilization are of critical importance.
Given this, a prudent policy stance is one of scenario planning and risk management, proactively taking steps that are flexible to different forms of disruption.
Those steps should be centered on a principle of promoting maximum participation—that is, individuals’ connection to meaningful participation in the economy.
Wage insurance, which replaces a portion of lost income when a laid-off worker takes a new, lower-paying job, was a shining element of the Trade Adjustment Assistance program.

items.title: Progressive AI agenda required for a balance between winners, losers: Economist Joseph E Stiglitz at HT Leadership Summit
points: According to Stiglitz, the ongoing AI boom has generated two key challenges for the global economy.
The first is whether the investments in AI will lead to expected returns, which in turn would determine if it creates a financial sector bubble that would eventually burst.
The second and more important challenge is striking a balance between the gainers and losers which AI will create in the global economy.
But whether the expected return in investment will be realised is a big doubt, the American economist said, pointing to the competitive nature of the sector.
“There are American companies in Silicon Valley doing AI frontier (models) that are using Chinese models (DeepSeek) to train their models, because they’re so cheap.

And we say, are they going to be very happy being a barista rather than the high-quality jobs they have today?” This is what makes it important to strike a balance between the winners and losers of AI, Stiglitz explained.

items.title: ‘AI speeding up drug design; next step is faster, cheaper medicines’: Siddhartha Mukherjee at HT Leadership Summit
points: Artificial intelligence is already cutting the time it takes to design new medicines from years to months, oncologist and author Siddhartha Mukherjee said on Saturday, but it must now make medicines faster, cheaper and better for patients if it is to prove…

“The single mitigating feature of AI is its capacity to produce transformative medicine,” Mukherjee, co-founder and chief executive of the drug-discovery company Manas AI, said at the 24th edition of the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit.
“Exhibit A of AI’s transformative power for human good is medicine.
To lay out his case, Mukherjee explained how arduous drug discovery can be.

There are 10 to the power of 24 possible small-molecule keys, far too many to try one by one, so modern drug design starts with the lock: find a “keyhole” in the target protein, then build a molecule from scratch to fit it.

items.title: Uttarakhand To Reopen 12 Closed Government ITIs From Next Academic Session
points: The Uttarakhand government has decided to reopen 12 non-operational Government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) from the next academic session.

The decision is aimed at expanding access to vocational and technical education and providing young people with more opportunities to develop skills that can help them find jobs or become self-employed.

Secretary of Skill Development and Employment C Ravi Shankar has directed the Director of Training and Employment, Nainital, to complete all necessary preparations and formalities within the given timeframe, officials said on Friday.
The reopening of these institutes is expected to benefit young people living in areas where the ITIs have remained non-functional.

With the institutes becoming operational again, students will be able to access skill-based training closer to their homes instead of travelling to other places for technical and vocational education.
According to Shankar, the decision is part of the state's efforts to strengthen skill development and make vocational training more accessible to young people.

points: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata has introduced a two-part plan for the country’s oldest and largest charity group: continue giving, but measure it by the results, and keep supporting Tata Sons’ investments in important national projects.
Speaking at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi on Saturday, the 70-year-old Tata Trusts chairman said the charitable institutions would have two distinct but complementary roles.
The second is through Tata Sons, to invest and nurture projects of national importance,” said Noel.

points: A US federal court has authorised the arrest of the tanker Atlantic Asphalt after the Port of New Orleans launched legal action seeking more than $1m in damages following the collision that sank American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage.

The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans filed the lawsuit in the Eastern District of Louisiana, naming the tanker, its owner Nave Shipping SA and OSM Thome’s Singapore-based Thome Ship Management as defendants.

Trump To Extend Shipping Waiver For Oil, Fertilizer For 90 Days
points: Nov 14, 2026 (Bloomberg) –President Donald Trump is giving energy companies and traders more time to transport oil and other commodities around the US on foreign-flagged ships, renewing a policy intended to lower fuel costs.

Trump has decided to extend by 90 days a waiver of mandates under the century-old Jones Act that otherwise require cargo carried between US ports to be transported on American-owned, -flagged and -operated vessels, according to a White House official…

Some 338 voyages have taken place on foreign vessels since Trump first waived Jones Act restrictions in March, including shipments of Texas crude to Pennsylvania and propane to Puerto Rico, according to government data analyzed by the Cato Institute.
The current waiver has helped enable the transport of some 13 million barrels of products, more than a third of which has been gasoline, with about 28% crude oil.
Trump’s Jones Act exemption has been the longest and broadest waiver of the law in more than seven decades.
